note: Questions on the seeded Raft course. `chapters` are seed chapter keys that should be retrieved and cited; `facts` are the points a good answer contains. Out-of-scope items expect the tutor to say the course doesn't cover it.

questions.question: Why does replicating a state machine reduce to agreeing on a log?
facts: deterministic replicas that apply the same commands in the same order end in the same state
so the problem becomes agreeing on the log's contents and order

questions.question: What does the FLP result mean for how Raft uses timing?
facts: no deterministic algorithm can guarantee consensus in a fully asynchronous system with even one crash
Raft never relies on timing for safety, only for liveness (making progress)

questions.question: Why does Raft use majority quorums?
facts: any two majorities of the same cluster overlap in at least one server
so anything a majority accepted is known to at least one member of every later majority

questions.question: How many server failures can a five-server Raft cluster tolerate, and why are odd sizes preferred?
facts: five servers tolerate two failures (majority is three)
adding a sixth server raises the majority to four without tolerating more failures

questions.question: In a network partition, what happens on the minority side?
facts: the minority side cannot form a majority, so it cannot elect a leader or commit entries
an old leader stranded there cannot commit; its uncommitted entries are later overwritten

questions.question: What is a term in Raft and what does a server do when it sees a higher term?
facts: terms are Raft's logical clock, numbered consecutively, each starting with an election
a server that sees a higher term updates its currentTerm and becomes a follower
at most one leader per term

questions.question: Which state must a Raft server persist before answering RPCs?
facts: currentTerm, votedFor and the log are persistent
commitIndex and lastApplied are volatile

questions.question: What are Raft's two RPCs used for?
facts: RequestVote is sent by candidates to gather votes
AppendEntries replicates log entries and doubles as the heartbeat

questions.question: When does a follower start an election?
facts: when its election timeout passes without hearing from a leader (no AppendEntries/heartbeat) or granting a vote
it increments its term, becomes a candidate, votes for itself and sends RequestVote to all

questions.question: Can two candidates both win an election in the same term?
facts: no: each server votes at most once per term and records the vote durably
a winner needs a majority and two majorities overlap (Election Safety)

questions.question: What is a split vote and does it threaten safety?
facts: several candidates split the votes so nobody gets a majority and the term ends with no leader
it only hurts liveness, never safety; a new election starts after another timeout

questions.question: Why are election timeouts randomized, and over what range?
facts: randomizing (for example 150 to 300 ms) makes it likely one server times out alone and wins before others start
the timeout is re-randomized on every reset

questions.question: What timing requirement must a Raft cluster meet?
facts: broadcastTime << electionTimeout << MTBF
otherwise leaders cannot hold leadership or elections never settle

questions.question: Why will a follower refuse to vote for some candidates even in a newer term?
facts: the election restriction: a voter refuses a candidate whose log is less up-to-date than its own
this guarantees every new leader already has every committed entry (Leader Completeness)

questions.question: How does Raft compare which log is more up-to-date?
facts: compare the term of the last entries first: the higher last term is more up-to-date
if the last terms are equal, the longer log is more up-to-date

questions.question: What is the AppendEntries consistency check?
facts: the leader sends PrevLogIndex and PrevLogTerm of the entry before the new ones
the follower rejects unless it has an entry at that index with that term

questions.question: What is the Log Matching property?
facts: if two logs have an entry with the same index and term, they store the same command
and the logs are identical in all entries before it (by induction from the consistency check)

questions.question: What are nextIndex and matchIndex, and how are they set after an election?
facts: nextIndex is the next entry to send to each follower; matchIndex the highest entry known replicated on it
after an election nextIndex is set to the leader's last index + 1 (and matchIndex to 0)
on a rejection the leader decrements nextIndex and retries

questions.question: How does a leader repair a follower whose log conflicts with its own?
facts: it backs nextIndex up until the consistency check passes
the follower deletes its conflicting suffix and takes the leader's entries
fast backup (conflict term/index) skips a whole term at a time

questions.question: Why can't a leader commit an entry from an earlier term just by counting replicas?
facts: Figure 8: an old-term entry on a majority can still be overwritten by a later leader
a leader only commits entries from its current term by counting replicas; earlier entries commit indirectly with them

questions.question: Why does a new Raft leader append a no-op entry?
facts: committing a current-term no-op commits everything before it
so the leader learns its true commitIndex right away (it is also used for linearizable reads)

questions.question: What is the difference between commitIndex and lastApplied?
facts: commitIndex is the highest entry known committed
lastApplied is the highest entry applied to the state machine; entries are applied up to commitIndex in order

questions.question: What does a Raft snapshot contain, and when does the leader send InstallSnapshot?
facts: the state machine state plus lastIncludedIndex and lastIncludedTerm (and the latest configuration)
servers snapshot independently
the leader sends InstallSnapshot when a follower needs entries it has discarded (nextIndex <= lastIncludedIndex)

questions.question: How does Raft change cluster membership safely?
facts: changing one server at a time keeps old and new majorities overlapping
joint consensus is the general alternative for larger changes
configurations are log entries

questions.question: How does a Raft-based service give exactly-once semantics and linearizable reads?
facts: clients tag commands with a client id and sequence number; the state machine deduplicates retries
before serving a read the leader confirms it is still leader (ReadIndex, a heartbeat round) and waits for its no-op to commit
